description: on today’s episode of BAKING SCIENCE, werr asking the age-old question: “why didnt my cookies turn out right?!” here are 4 of the most common reasons and why. plua stay ‘til the end to see my PERFECT COOKIEEEEE #bakingscience #cookiescience #cookierecipe
transcript: One of the most common questions I get asked is why didn't my cookies turn out right? So here I'm breaking down four of the most common mistakes that happen when baking cookies. First, overpacking your flour. If your cookies turned out thick and didn't spread as much then you probably overpacked your flour. Always spoon your flour into a measuring cup then level it off with a back of a knife so you don't end up over measuring. Secondly, not chilling your dough. If your cookies are too flat and not as chewy it might be because you didn't chill your dough. Not all cookie recipes require chilling dough but when they do you have to do it otherwise your cookie will end up spreading too much. Third, over mixing. If your cookie tastes tough and bready you might have overmix your dough. Once you add flour into your cookie dough you want to mix that dough as little as possible. This is because flour contains gluten that basically firm up the more they're mixed. Instead mix your cookies as little as possible to keep them chewy and soft. Last, overcooked. So often I hear people say their cookie ended up dry and crumbly and one likely culprit is you probably overcooked your cookie. Ovens are notoriously finicky and often run hotter than the temperature says they are. So to prevent this I always set a timer that's slightly less than the recipe calls for it and take my cookies out when they look slightly underdone because they'll continue to bake as they cool on the pan. And if you want to see what I think is a perfect cookie here it is. It has the right amount of flour that was just barely mixed. It was chilled for an hour and I took it out when it was just slightly underdone.
